A scanned, image-only PDF blocks TutorChat go-live because the ingestion pipeline depends on an embedded text layer. The KnowledgeHub expects documents to have a text layer before ingestion; if a document is image-only, the system cannot index the text or generate citation anchors [NL-018#NL-018-S05]. The standard PDF parser fails to detect text layers in image-only documents, resulting in empty indexes unless external OCR pre-processing is applied [NL-031#NL-031-S04]. When customers sneak raw TIFFs/PNGs inside PDF containers, the parser fails to find text and produces a generic import error [NL-021#NL-021-S02]. This leads to empty document models or TutorChat being unable to generate citations [NL-029#NL-029-S05].

At retrieval time, TutorChat either returns an answer with no source citations because it cannot find text offsets, or the citation points to the entire document — for example, page 1 of a 250-page PDF — rather than the exact section [NL-021#NL-021-S02]. The failed extraction can also cause omitted content, as in the scanned neonatal ventilator protocol where TutorChat missed two critical alarm threshold steps because text extraction failed on that page [NL-018#NL-018-S05].

Because automated OCR is unavailable, customers or the CS team must manually OCR pre-process the files, adding weeks to onboarding [NL-010#NL-010-S06]. Northstar Financial’s pilot kickoff was delayed by three weeks due to external OCR processing [NL-010#NL-010-S06]. BrightPath Healthcare experienced the longest onboarding time, 9.5 weeks, because of manual formatting checks on scanned compliance files [NL-031#NL-031-S04].

At the reliability gate, the current indexing system lacks advanced OCR, so scanned PDFs return incomplete citations and fail the go-live validation threshold of 85% citation correctness [NL-031#NL-031-S04]. Compliance officers refuse to sign off on a general rollout because medical staff cannot verify answers when citations are missing or point to a 200-page document [NL-021#NL-021-S02]. Consequently, BrightPath remains restricted to its initial 100-user group and cannot move to the full 6,500 employees until the scanned-PDF citation problem is solved [NL-021#NL-021-S02].
